overview.problem: The reconnect wizard answers '/' and the playlist-reconstruction screen answers '/reconstruct', and the only path between them is one ui.link at the bottom of the wizard page reading 'Reconstruct playlists from another collection' with no link back. Nothing on either page names the other operation and nothing says which one is open. The reconstruct screen is the operator's own critical use case yet it is the one reached by scrolling past a four-step stepper. The design set already carries the shell the operator wants: Main.dc.html's header bar - a brand mark, a divider and a strip whose selected item takes the SURFACE_4 ground, an inset border and TEXT ink - while the app draws no header at all.
overview.approach:
The app gains a header bar carrying two tabs, applied to both routes from the one preamble both routes already call. Eight things are settled rather than left implicit.

The routes swap and the wizard takes '/reconnect' (DL-129). 'Default selected' is not a rendering state: a tab is a link the browser follows, so the tab selected on open is whichever one names the route '/' resolves to. The places naming the old arrangement are produced by a recorded command rather than by recall (DL-145), because two rounds of hand-listing each missed one: git --no-pager grep -nE over a pattern matching a slash, then recon, then struct or nect, then any character that is not a letter, digit, hyphen or underscore - run at each repository root, and in the tool repository over traktor_nml, tests, design, tools and CLAUDE.md so the historical plan documents under docs/ stay outside it. The trailing character class is what does the work: without it reconnect_run.py, reconnect_render.py and design/reconnect-wizard/ flood the output, and the same pattern with no pathspec returns 107 lines against the recorded command's 9. That command returns the same 9 lines with MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 set and unset, measured both ways, so the variable is a precaution against a different shape of the search and not a property of this one. The shape it guards reproduces exactly: git --no-pager grep -n -F "/reconstruct" returns nothing at exit 1 while the same command under MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 returns 34 lines, because a bare leading-slash argument is rewritten into a Windows path before git sees it - the probe python -c "import sys;print(sys.argv[1:])" -F "/reconstruct" prints the rewritten path, and the -E pattern, carrying parentheses and a bracket class, is passed through unchanged. What it returns in the tool repository is app.py:207's ui.link, app.py:1215's comment, app.py:1221's docstring, app.py:1232's registration, tests/test_gui_conflict_page_controls.py:1's docstring, Specs.dc.html:260's section heading and traktor_nml/README.md:880 and :1096 - three of them in a comment, a test docstring and prose, where the AST guard of DL-144 cannot see them, since an ast.Constant walk reads string literals and never a '#' comment. CLAUDE.md:25 matches the pattern, reads 'rewrite/reconnect/splice', and is recorded as reviewed and excluded. The wizard-at-root side is app.py:187, app.py:169's docstring and traktor_nml/gui/__main__.py, whose docstring reads 'Entry point that starts the reconnect wizard' and whose ui.run passes title='traktor-nml-tool - reconnect wizard' with native=True, so the product's own window opens whatever '/' resolves to. The entry point's title reads 'traktor-nml-tool' (DL-140), because the window holds both operations and the header's selected tab names the open one. That '/reconnect' is unclaimed is established by enumeration (DL-130): traktor_nml/ holds exactly two @ui.page registrations; nicegui mounts only '/_nicegui_ws/', '/_nicegui/{version}/...' and '/favicon.ico'; no '/reconnect' route string exists in the sources. '/reconstruct' is then registered by nothing and answers the framework's own 404 (DL-141): keeping it alive by a second registration or a redirect means two paths answering one page, which is the shape this change removes, and what makes the 404 safe is the enumeration rather than a redirect. Re-running both commands after the change is an acceptance criterion, and any hit the plan does not name is reported rather than silently changed.

The header carries the brand mark, the divider and the tab strip, and no .task element (DL-131). Main.dc.html puts .task beside the progress rail to name the screen; the tab strip names both operations and marks which is open, so the selected tab already carries that name and a .task beside it would name the screen twice from two sources with no rule saying which wins. Because this is a cross-screen contract rather than one artboard's layout it is drawn into design/reconnect-wizard/Specs.dc.html first, per the design set's own precedence rule (DL-071), and Main.dc.html keeps every byte.

A tab is an anchor whose href is the route it names (DL-132), so each operation keeps its own URL and the browser performs a real page load. The selected one carries aria-current='page' and wizard-tab-selected. The mechanism that reads that back is named rather than assumed (DL-133, DL-139): the suite runs on the system interpreter, where `import nicegui` raises ModuleNotFoundError and tests/test_gui_view_boundary.py records that app.py is untested by interaction because no pytest harness drives rendered DOM - so a guard claiming to render the header would quietly degrade to a source read or a MagicMock call log. Instead the tab table and the selection rule move into a nicegui-free module, traktor_nml/gui/navigation.py, beside review_model.py and wizard_state.py, and three mechanisms carry the rule with their reach stated. One: a pure unit guard runs navigation.header_tabs with no framework present and resolves all four cases - right tab, wrong tab, both, none - and cannot establish that app.py uses the result. Two: a recording stub, in the register tests/test_gui_module_imports.py already establishes by installing minimal nicegui and webview stand-ins into sys.modules and restoring them in a finally, records each ui.link's target and its handle's .classes() and .props() strings, calls app.py's header builder per route, and asserts the collected marker targets equal exactly that route - it establishes that app.py emits two links in table order and marks the right one, and cannot establish that nicegui renders an anchor or that the class survives Quasar's layers. Three: the served-page gate run, the only mechanism that reads the rendered DOM. In every mechanism the comparison is equality against exactly one route - never membership, never any() - and a second marker on one anchor counts. An AST guard in the register tests/test_gui_view_boundary.py uses keeps app.py free of any route literal outside its two ui.page arguments and of either tab label (DL-144). The header renders from _page_chrome, which takes the active route (DL-134), because that function is already the single preamble both routes call so a second route cannot drift from the wizard's theme (DL-078, DL-085).

The milestone boundary follows the coupling a guard already reports (DL-147): tests/test_gui_theme.py:333 asserts every .wizard-* class page_stylesheet() defines appears in app.py's source, and the five header and tab classes have exactly one consumer - the header builder - so theme.py and tests/test_gui_theme.py sit in the milestone that writes app.py. Parking a class in _KNOWN_UNATTACHED_CLASSES to clear a milestone gate is refused by that list's own comment at tests/test_gui_theme.py:321-330, which says its single entry is there because no milestone builds a consumer for it and that entries are named one at a time so a forgotten class cannot hide under the same excuse. navigation.py keeps a milestone of its own because it imports no framework and waits on no consumer. The five header and tab rules are built in theme.py from tokens it already carries - SURFACE_2, SURFACE_4, BORDER, BORDER_STRONG, TEXT, TEXT_FAINT and the type scale (DL-135) - so no hex reaches app.py. Every note inside page_stylesheet is a /* */ block (DL-136): a '#' line inside that string is an ID selector whose block is the rule following it, so the next rule is swallowed and nothing raises. app.py is the one CRLF file in the package at 1612 CRLF and zero bare LF while theme.py, __main__.py, navigation.py and the tests are LF, and every edit preserves that with newline='' and a byte check (DL-142).

No gate script takes a code change (DL-137), established by reading each end to end and by running the same enumeration over that repository. The enumeration returns six lines there - .gitignore:10, reconstruct_fixture.py:1 and :190, and serve_reconstruct.py:1, :10 and :16 - and serve_w002.py's docstring and README.md:29 are not among them, since neither carries the token; those two are in M-004 on the strength of reading them, which is how a file naming a port and a page without naming a route is found at all. serve_w002.py holds no route string at all; serve_reconstruct.py's only ones sit in its module docstring at lines 1, 10 and 16; reconstruct_fixture.py names the screen by its route at lines 1 and 190; the README's serve_w002.py table row at line 29 is the only line naming port 8115, and there is no line-by-line driving order there to edit; and .gitignore line 10's comment describes what 'a /reconstruct gate run' writes. Every executable body stands and the change is prose in those five files. SCREEN-READER-PASS.md is excluded and keeps every byte (DL-146): its line 4 reads as a procedure, but line 109 of the same file says it is 'kept as a record of the pass that ran on 2026-08-29, not as an invitation to run another' and line 107 puts accessibility work out of scope for this version, so the later and more specific statement governs. Its line 75 Edge launch is the launch that pass actually used, and the reading it produced - docs/2026-08-29-w004-focus-ring-record.md - is frozen byte for byte here, so repointing line 75 would make the two files disagree about what was driven and aim a do-not-run procedure at a route no recorded pass ever used. That record and docs/2026-08-28-w002-browser-record.md keep every byte; the run this plan takes drives '/', '/reconnect' and '/reconstruct' and is written into a new dated record (DL-138, DL-143).

traktor_nml/README.md's own high-water mark reads DL-128, confirmed by reading the file, so this plan mints DL-129 through DL-146. Per the task spec it carries no code_changes and no waves: the four milestones run in order M-001, M-002, M-003, M-004.

decisions.decision: The reconstruct page answers '/' and the reconnect wizard answers '/reconnect'
decisions.reasoning: The operator's settled requirement is that reconstruct is the leftmost tab and the route the app opens on -> a default selected tab is not a rendering state but the route '/' resolves to because a tab is a link the browser follows -> swapping the two @ui.page registrations is the mechanism and every place naming the old arrangement is found by the recorded enumeration of DL-145 rather than by recall. In the tool repository the enumeration returns app.py:207's ui.link; app.py:1215's COMMENT reading 'The /reconstruct page renders the rows the same run'; app.py:1221's docstring; app.py:1232's registration; tests/test_gui_conflict_page_controls.py:1's docstring 'Guards what the /reconstruct page's conflict surface delegates'; design/reconnect-wizard/Specs.dc.html:260's section heading 'Splice conflicts - /reconstruct'; and traktor_nml/README.md:880 and :1096. CLAUDE.md:25 matches the pattern and is not a route - it reads 'rewrite/reconnect/splice' - and is recorded as reviewed and excluded. The wizard-at-root side is app.py:187's registration; app.py:169's docstring 'Registers the wizard's single page at /'; and traktor_nml/gui/__main__.py whose docstring reads 'Entry point that starts the reconnect wizard' and whose ui.run passes title='traktor-nml-tool - reconnect wizard' with native=True so the product's own window opens whatever '/' resolves to. The gate repository's hits are enumerated in DL-137. Three of these sit in a comment a test docstring and markdown prose where no AST guard can see them which is why the enumeration is a text grep and DL-145 records the command.

decisions.decision: '/reconnect' is unclaimed and the enumeration of route owners is the evidence
decisions.reasoning: A second route can only collide with a path something else already answers -> the owners of paths in this app are the @ui.page registrations in the package and the routes nicegui mounts for itself -> grep for 'ui.page(' over traktor_nml/ returns exactly two registrations app.py:187 '/' and app.py:1232 '/reconstruct' and neither is '/reconnect'; nicegui's own mounts read from nicegui/nicegui.py as '/_nicegui_ws/' '/_nicegui/{version}/...' and '/favicon.ico'; a grep for the literal '/reconnect' across the tree's .py .md and .html sources outside .venv build/lib and dist/ returns prose about the reconnect wizard and the design directory name and no route string. The path is therefore free and the guard that keeps it free is the route-set assertion in M-003.

decisions.decision: The header carries the brand mark the divider and the two tabs and no .task element
decisions.reasoning: Main.dc.html's header is brand + bar + .task on the left and the .rail progress strip on the right where .task names the screen -> the tab strip names both operations and marks which one is open so the selected tab already carries the screen's name -> a .task beside it would name the screen twice from two sources that can disagree with no rule saying which wins. The header therefore renders .brand and .bar and the tab strip. Because this is a cross-screen contract rather than one screen's layout it is written into design/reconnect-wizard/Specs.dc.html first per the design set's own precedence rule (DL-071).

decisions.decision: A tab is an anchor the browser follows and its href is the route it names
decisions.reasoning: The two operations are separate pages registered at separate routes and share no pipeline -> a client-side toggle would render one page for two routes and cost each operation the URL it is reachable by -> each tab is a ui.link whose target is that operation's own route so the browser performs a page load and the address bar carries the route. The tab strip is a nav element labelled Sections holding exactly two anchors: '/' labelled Reconstruct playlists first and '/reconnect' labelled Reconnect wizard second.

decisions.decision: The selected tab is marked by aria-current='page' and wizard-tab-selected and three mechanisms of stated reach read it back
decisions.reasoning: A selected state expressed only as a colour is a state no guard can read and a guard asserting the marker merely appears passes while the wrong tab carries it -> the state must name WHICH tab carries it AND the guard reading it must be a mechanism that exists on the interpreter the suite runs on -> the system interpreter has no nicegui (import nicegui raises ModuleNotFoundError) and tests/test_gui_view_boundary.py records that app.py is untested by interaction because no pytest harness drives rendered DOM, so a guard claiming to render the header would degrade to a source read or a MagicMock call log. Three mechanisms carry the rule and each states what it establishes and what it cannot. Mechanism one is a pure unit guard over navigation.header_tabs which computes the tab records with no framework present: it establishes that for each route exactly one record is selected and it is the record whose route equals the active route in the order the table declares - the four cases resolve here - and it cannot establish that app.py uses the result. Mechanism two is a recording stub following the register tests/test_gui_module_imports.py already establishes - minimal nicegui and webview stand-ins installed into sys.modules for the duration of the test - whose ui.link records its label and target and whose returned handle records its .classes() and .props() strings: it calls app.py's header builder for each route and collects the recorded targets the targets carrying aria-current='page' and the targets carrying wizard-tab-selected, establishing that app.py emits two links in table order with the right targets and marks exactly the right one, and it cannot establish that nicegui renders ui.link as an anchor or that the class survives Quasar's layers. Mechanism three is the served-page gate run which reads the rendered DOM and is the only one that establishes what a browser has. In every mechanism the collected markers are compared by equality against exactly the one route under test - never by membership and never by any() - and a second marker on the same anchor counts, so the wrong tab both tabs and no tab each fail.

decisions.decision: _page_chrome renders the header and takes the active route as its argument
decisions.reasoning: _page_chrome is already the one preamble both routes call precisely so a second route cannot drift from the wizard's theme (DL-078 DL-085) -> a header rendered anywhere else would be two call sites that can disagree about the tab set -> _page_chrome takes the active route and renders the header after the stylesheet is installed so both pages carry one header built from one tab table. The tab table is a module-level constant of route-and-label pairs and the active route selects from it rather than each page naming its own tabs.

decisions.decision: The header and tab rules are built in theme.py from tokens it already carries
decisions.reasoning: theme.py holds the stylesheet and imports no nicegui (DL-069) and app.py carries no hex literal which tests/test_gui_theme.py enforces by scanning app.py's source -> a rule expressed in app.py would either repeat a colour or be untestable below the boundary -> the header bar the tab and the selected tab are classes in page_stylesheet built from GROUND SURFACE_2 SURFACE_4 BORDER BORDER_STRONG TEXT TEXT_FAINT and the existing type scale. The selected tab follows Main.dc.html's .st.now treatment: the SURFACE_4 ground the inset BORDER_STRONG border and TEXT ink at weight 600. No colour is added to theme.py and no hex reaches app.py.

decisions.decision: page_stylesheet carries no '#' comment and a guard asserts the count of rules the stylesheet defines
decisions.reasoning: The stylesheet is one f-string of CSS and CSS has no '#' comment form -> a '#' line inside it parses as an ID selector whose block is the text following it so the rule after it is swallowed and no parse error is raised anywhere -> every note inside page_stylesheet is written in /* */ form and a guard asserts that each header and tab class name appears as a selector at the start of a rule in the returned string and that the string holds no line whose first non-space character is '#'. The mutation that makes it fail replaces one /* */ note with a '#' line.

decisions.decision: No gate script takes a code change and the prose in five gate files takes the routes
decisions.reasoning: A gate script that names a route would fail on the swap and one that does not would keep serving whatever app.py registers -> every gate file was read and the DL-145 enumeration was run over that repository too, the enumeration returning six lines - .gitignore:10, reconstruct_fixture.py:1 and :190, and serve_reconstruct.py:1, :10 and :16 - while serve_w002.py's docstring and README.md:29 carry no such token and are here on the strength of reading them instead -> serve_w002.py calls gui_app.build_wizard() and ui.run(port=8115) and holds no route string at all; serve_reconstruct.py calls gui_app.build_wizard() and ui.run(port=8116) and its only route strings sit in its module docstring at lines 1 10 and 16; reconstruct_fixture.py names the screen by its route in its module docstring at line 1 and in a function docstring at line 190; the README's serve_w002.py table row at line 29 is the only line in that file naming port 8115 and there is no line-by-line driving order in it to edit; and .gitignore line 10's comment describes the files 'a /reconstruct gate run' writes. Every executable body stands and what changes is prose in those five files. serve_w002.py stays CRLF and the rest LF as the gate's own '* -text' setting preserves. SCREEN-READER-PASS.md is a record and is excluded by DL-146. The gate README's file table naming five scripts and not serve_reconstruct.py predates this change and stands.

decisions.decision: Acceptance is a served-page gate run that opens both routes and reads the header back off each
decisions.reasoning: A gui/ defect has only ever been found by serving the page (DL-084) and the duplicate-entry defect surfaced there after a green suite -> a header is exactly the class of change a stylesheet layer or a framework default can defeat while the unit guards stay green -> the gate run serves the app from C:\codex\traktor-nml-tool-gate opens 'http://localhost:8115/' and 'http://localhost:8115/reconnect' and reads back per route which anchor hrefs the header holds which one carries aria-current='page' and the computed background of the selected tab against theme.SURFACE_4. The run is recorded in a new dated record under docs/ rather than into either existing record.

decisions.decision: The tab table and the selection rule sit in traktor_nml/gui/navigation.py below the nicegui boundary
decisions.reasoning: The rule that decides which tab is selected is the one thing in this change a defect can silently invert -> a rule expressed inside a @ui.page body can only be read back through a framework the suite does not have -> the table of route-and-label pairs and the function that turns an active route into tab records move into a new nicegui-free module beside review_model.py wizard_state.py and conflict_model.py which are already model modules below the boundary that tests/test_gui_view_boundary.py enforces. header_tabs(active_route) returns one record per table row carrying the route the label whether it is selected the class string and the aria-current value or None so the selection rule is a pure computation a guard runs directly. navigation.py is LF and imports no nicegui; app.py renders what it returns and decides nothing.

decisions.decision: __main__.py's window title and docstring name the application rather than one of its operations
decisions.reasoning: __main__.py calls ui.run(title='traktor-nml-tool - reconnect wizard' native=True) and native mode opens whatever '/' resolves to -> after the swap '/' is the reconstruct page so the product's own window would open the reconstruct screen under a title naming the wizard -> the title reads 'traktor-nml-tool' and the module docstring states that the entry point starts the application. The window holds both operations and the header's selected tab names the one that is open so a title naming either operation contradicts the header on the other route. The docstring's second paragraph - why this lives here rather than in commands/ - stands word for word. __main__.py is LF at zero CRLF and is written as such.

decisions.decision: '/reconstruct' is registered by nothing and answers nicegui's own 404
decisions.reasoning: A path that answered a page and then answers nothing is a dead link for any bookmark or procedure still holding it -> the two ways to keep it alive are registering the page at both paths or redirecting one to the other and both mean two paths answering for one page which is the shape this change exists to remove -> nothing is registered at '/reconstruct' and a request for it gets the framework's own 404. What makes that safe is the enumeration rather than a redirect: every reference to '/reconstruct' in either repository is named in DL-129 and updated in the same change so no procedure this project owns still holds the path. A bookmark a person kept is outside what either repository can fix and a redirect would not tell that person the app was rearranged.

decisions.decision: Every edit to app.py preserves its 100% CRLF and every other touched Python file its LF
decisions.reasoning: app.py is the one Python file in the package written CRLF throughout at 1612 CRLF and zero bare LF while theme.py __main__.py the model modules and the tests are LF -> an editor or a helper that normalises on write silently converts the file and the diff swallows the whole module -> every read and write of app.py passes newline='' and a guard asserts app.py's bytes hold zero bare LF and that navigation.py __main__.py and theme.py hold zero CRLF. The gate's serve_w002.py is CRLF and its other scripts LF under that repository's own '* -text' setting and a byte check reports each after the edit.

decisions.decision: The served-page gate run drives three URLs and reads back what the DOM has
decisions.reasoning: The unit mechanisms stop at what app.py emits and cannot see a framework defeat a rule -> the rendered page is the only place the header's anchors their hrefs the marker and the painted colour exist together -> the run serves the app and opens http://localhost:8115/ and http://localhost:8115/reconnect and reads back per route the header's anchor hrefs in order which single href carries aria-current='page' which single href carries wizard-tab-selected and the computed background of the selected tab against theme.SURFACE_4 and the computed colour of an unselected tab against theme.TEXT_FAINT with a matches-or-differs verdict per named surface. It also opens http://localhost:8115/reconstruct and records the status the framework returns for a path nothing registers. The run is written into a new dated record; the two existing browser records keep every byte.

decisions.decision: The header builder is the only place in app.py naming a route or a tab label and the AST guard reaching that sees string literals only
decisions.reasoning: Two places naming a route is the shape that lets one page carry a tab set the other does not -> the table sits in navigation.py so any route string left in app.py is a second source -> app.py imports the table calls navigation.header_tabs(active_route) and passes each record's route to ui.link's target its class string to .classes() and its aria-current to .props(). An AST guard in the register tests/test_gui_view_boundary.py already uses asserts that the only string literals matching a route shape in app.py are the two @ui.page arguments and that neither tab label appears in app.py at all. Its reach is stated rather than assumed: an ast.Constant walk sees string literals and a docstring which is one and it does NOT see a '#' comment - app.py:1215's comment naming the old route is invisible to it and was found by the DL-145 text grep instead. The guard establishes source-level single sourcing for literals; the enumeration covers comments and prose; neither establishes behaviour which is what DL-139's three mechanisms are for.

decisions.decision: The enumeration of route references is produced by a recorded command and acceptance is re-running it
decisions.reasoning: Two rounds of hand-listing the places that name a route each missed one -> a list written by recall is not evidence and a later reader cannot tell a complete list from an incomplete one -> the enumeration is a command written into the plan and into traktor_nml/README.md so it can be re-run: git --no-pager grep -nE with the pattern matching a slash then recon then struct or nect then any character that is not a letter digit hyphen or underscore or end of line; run at the root of each repository and in the tool repository restricted to traktor_nml tests design tools and CLAUDE.md so the historical plan documents under docs/ - records of plans already taken - stay outside it. The load-bearing part is the trailing character class: without it traktor_nml/reconnect_run.py traktor_nml/reconnect_render.py and design/reconnect-wizard/ flood the output, and the same pattern with no pathspec at all returns 107 lines against the 9 the recorded command returns. Measured in Git Bash at C:/codex/traktor-nml-tool: the recorded command returns 9 lines and returns the same 9 with MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 set and unset, so that variable is no part of what makes it work. It is a precaution against a different shape of the same search rather than a property of this one, and that shape reproduces exactly: git --no-pager grep -n -F "/reconstruct" returns nothing and exits 1, while MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 git --no-pager grep -n -F "/reconstruct" returns 34 lines. The cause is visible one level down - python -c "import sys;print(sys.argv[1:])" -F "/reconstruct" prints ['-F' 'C:/Users/marcu/AppData/Local/Programs/Git/reconstruct'] and the same invocation under MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 prints ['-F' '/reconstruct'] - so a bare leading-slash argument is rewritten into a Windows path before git sees it. The -E pattern escapes that conversion because it carries parentheses a pipe a bracket class and a dollar, which the same probe confirms is passed through unchanged. A fixed-string search for a route therefore reads as a clean tree while the tree is full of hits, which is why the recorded command is the -E one. Acceptance is that re-running it in both repositories after the change returns only the lines this plan names as intentionally keeping the old token and that any other hit is reported rather than silently changed.

decisions.decision: SCREEN-READER-PASS.md is a record and keeps every byte
decisions.reasoning: The file's line 4 says it is written down so the next pass is a re-run rather than a rediscovery which reads as a procedure -> line 109 of the same file says it is 'kept as a record of the pass that ran on 2026-08-29 not as an invitation to run another' and 'Do not fetch NVDA for this project' and line 107 says accessibility work is out of scope for this version -> the later and more specific statement governs and the file is a record. Its line 75 Edge launch at http://localhost:8115 is the launch the 2026-08-29 pass actually used and the reading it produced is docs/2026-08-29-w004-focus-ring-record.md which this plan freezes byte for byte; rewriting line 75 would make the two files disagree about what was driven and would point a do-not-run procedure at a route no recorded pass ever used. The file is therefore untouched and sits in no milestone's files. What a later session needs is in the places that are live: the gate README's serve_w002.py row names the wizard's URL and traktor_nml/README.md carries the route statement. This entry also records the citation error it corrects - the earlier reading cited line 4 alone for a classification line 109 contradicts.

decisions.decision: A stylesheet class and its only consumer land in one milestone
decisions.reasoning: tests/test_gui_theme.py:333 test_every_wizard_class_reaches_app_py asserts every .wizard-* class page_stylesheet() defines appears in app.py's source -> the five header and tab classes have exactly one consumer and it is the header builder in app.py -> a milestone adding the rules without the builder cannot go green, so theme.py and tests/test_gui_theme.py sit in the milestone that writes app.py rather than in one of their own. The alternative - entering a class in _KNOWN_UNATTACHED_CLASSES to get past a milestone gate - is refused by that list's own comment at tests/test_gui_theme.py:321-330, which says its single entry is there because no milestone in that plan builds a consumer for it and that entries are named one at a time rather than by a pattern precisely so a genuinely forgotten class cannot slip through under the same excuse; a class whose consumer lands one milestone later is not an unattached class. What is left in its own milestone is navigation.py and its guards, which import no framework and have no consumer to wait for, so the boundary follows the coupling the guard reports rather than the file types.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Keep the bottom link and add tabs beside it
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Two ways to reach one page, and the link is the thing the operator asked to replace

rejected_alternatives.alternative: A client-side tab toggle rendering both operations on one page
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: The two share no pipeline and '/reconstruct' is a separate route for that reason, as app.py's own docstring records; a toggle would also cost each operation its own URL

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Redirect '/' to the reconstruct route and leave the wizard registered at '/' as well
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Two paths answering for one page, and a redirect the gate has to know about anyway

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Adopt the whole shell - header, footer action bar and card treatment
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Rejected by the operator as scope for this change

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Keep Main.dc.html's .task element in the app header beside the tabs

risks.risk: A note written with '#' inside page_stylesheet's string parses as an ID selector and swallows the rule after it with no parse error anywhere

risks.risk: Quasar's own layer defeats a header rule at every specificity because its !important sits in the layer the page orders last

risks.risk: An editor rewrites app.py's line endings and the file stops being 100% CRLF

risks.risk: A selected-tab guard is written against a rendered DOM the suite cannot produce and degrades to a source read or a MagicMock call log that passes while the wrong tab is marked

risks.risk: The product's own entry point opens the reconstruct screen under a window title naming the reconnect wizard
risks.mitigation: __main__.py's ui.run title reads 'traktor-nml-tool' and a guard asserts neither the title nor the docstring names one operation; the served run records the title the native window carries

risks.risk: The gate's reconstruct procedure opens a route nothing answers and reads a 404 as a broken page

risks.risk: A route enumeration written as a fixed-string search - git grep -n -F "/reconstruct" - returns nothing and exits 1 because the MSYS layer rewrites the bare leading-slash argument into a Windows path before git sees it, and the empty output reads as a clean tree
risks.mitigation: The recorded command is the -E form, whose pattern carries parentheses a pipe a bracket class and a dollar and is passed through unchanged - it returns the same 9 lines with MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 set or unset. The plan records the failing invocation its 0-line exit-1 result and the 34 lines the same search returns under MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1, so a zero-hit run in a tree known to hold the Specs section heading is read as a broken invocation rather than a clean tree

invisible_knowledge.system: The GUI is a nicegui app whose two screens are two @ui.page registrations in traktor_nml/gui/app.py. theme.py sits below the nicegui boundary (DL-069): it imports no nicegui, names every colour and size as a module constant, and returns the whole stylesheet from page_stylesheet() as one f-string that app.py installs through ui.add_head_html. app.py carries no hex literal - tests/test_gui_theme.py enforces that by scanning app.py's source - and every class the stylesheet defines must reach app.py, which another guard in the same module enforces in the other direction. The design set under design/reconnect-wizard/ is committed primary source (DL-071): Specs.dc.html is the cross-screen contract and the artboards are the screens, with the set's own rule that a disagreement is fixed in Specs first, and reconnect-wizard.html is a gitignored bundle seeded from those sources. tests/test_gui_theme.py reads the design set at test time, so every colour an artboard paints and every px font size it specifies must already be named in theme.py. The suite runs on the system interpreter, which has neither nicegui nor pywebview: tests/test_gui_view_boundary.py reads gui/ by AST walk and states that app.py is deliberately untested by interaction because no pytest harness drives rendered DOM, while tests/test_gui_module_imports.py installs minimal nicegui and webview stand-ins into sys.modules - the nicegui stub answering arbitrary attribute access with a MagicMock except ui.dialog, which must be a real class because file_picker.py subclasses it - performs a genuine import of each gui/ module and restores sys.modules in a finally. A @ui.page body does not run at import time under that stub, only at request time, so anything a unit guard needs to read must be reachable without a request.

readme_entries.content:
# 2026-09-03 header tabs

The app draws no header. The reconnect wizard answers `/`, the playlist-reconstruction screen answers `/reconstruct`, and the only path between them is one `ui.link` at the bottom of the wizard page with no link back; nothing on either page names the other operation or says which one is open. This plan gives both routes one header bar - the brand mark, a divider and two tabs - built from Main.dc.html's own header treatment, with the reconstruct screen answering `/` and the reconnect wizard moving to `/reconnect`.

| File | What |
| --- | --- |
| `plan.json` | The plan: overview, DL-129 through DL-147, and four milestones with their files, requirements, acceptance criteria, tests and code intents. No code_changes and no waves. |
| `context.json` | The task spec, the operator's settled decisions, the constraints, the entry points and the invisible knowledge the plan was designed against. |

Six things it settles rather than leaves implicit.

**The routes, and how the enumeration was produced.** The wizard's path is `/reconnect`. The places naming the old arrangement come from a recorded command rather than from recall, because two rounds of hand-listing each missed one: `git --no-pager grep -nE` over a pattern matching a slash, `recon`, `struct` or `nect`, then any character that is not a letter, digit, hyphen or underscore. The trailing class is what does the work: without it `reconnect_run.py`, `reconnect_render.py` and `design/reconnect-wizard/` flood the output, and the same pattern with no pathspec returns 107 lines against the recorded command's 9. Measured both ways, that command returns the same 9 lines with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` set and unset, so the variable is a precaution rather than a requirement here - it guards a different shape of the search, which does reproduce: `git --no-pager grep -n -F "/reconstruct"` returns nothing at exit 1 while the same command under `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` returns 34 lines, because a bare leading-slash argument is rewritten into a Windows path before git sees it. It returns `app.py`'s link, comment, docstring and registration, `tests/test_gui_conflict_page_controls.py`'s docstring, `Specs.dc.html`'s section heading and two lines of `traktor_nml/README.md` - three of them in a comment, a test docstring and prose, invisible to the AST guard, which reads string literals and never a `#` comment. `CLAUDE.md:25` matches and is not a route; it is recorded as reviewed. The wizard-at-root side is `app.py`'s registration and docstring and `traktor_nml/gui/__main__.py`, whose `ui.run(title="traktor-nml-tool - reconnect wizard", native=True)` opens whatever `/` resolves to. In the gate repository it returns six lines - `.gitignore:10`, `reconstruct_fixture.py:1` and `:190`, and `serve_reconstruct.py:1`, `:10` and `:16`. `serve_w002.py`'s docstring and `README.md:29` carry no such token and are in scope on the strength of reading them, not of the enumeration. Re-running both commands is an acceptance criterion. That `/reconnect` is unclaimed is established by enumeration: exactly two `@ui.page` registrations, nicegui's own mounts, and no `/reconnect` route string anywhere in the sources.

**The entry point.** The native window title reads `traktor-nml-tool`: the window holds both operations and the header's selected tab names the open one, so a title naming either operation contradicts the header on the other route.

**`/reconstruct` after the swap.** Nothing registers it and it answers the framework's own 404. A second registration or a redirect means two paths answering one page, which is the shape this change removes; what makes the 404 safe is the enumeration, not a redirect.

**The `.task` element.** It does not appear in the app header - the selected tab names the screen, and `.task` beside it would name it twice from a source that can disagree. The contract is drawn into `design/reconnect-wizard/Specs.dc.html` first, per DL-071.

**What a tab is, and how the selected state is read.** A tab is an anchor whose `href` is that operation's route; the selected one carries `aria-current="page"` and `wizard-tab-selected`. The mechanism is named rather than assumed: the suite runs on the system interpreter, where `import nicegui` raises `ModuleNotFoundError` and `tests/test_gui_view_boundary.py` records that no pytest harness drives rendered DOM, so a guard claiming to render the header would degrade to a source read or a MagicMock call log. The tab table and the selection rule therefore sit in a nicegui-free `traktor_nml/gui/navigation.py`, and three mechanisms carry the rule with their reach stated: a pure unit guard over `header_tabs` resolving all four cases (right tab, wrong tab, both, none); a recording stub in the register `tests/test_gui_module_imports.py` already establishes, reading the targets and props app.py hands `ui.link`; and the served-page run, the only one that reads the rendered DOM. Every comparison is equality against exactly one route - never membership, never `any()`.

**The gate.** Neither script takes a code change: `serve_w002.py` holds no route string and `serve_reconstruct.py`'s only ones sit in its docstring. Prose changes in five gate files - the two docstrings, the README's `serve_w002.py` table row at line 29 (the only line naming port 8115; there is no line-by-line driving order there), and `.gitignore`'s fixture comment. `SCREEN-READER-PASS.md` keeps every byte: line 4 reads as a procedure, but line 109 of the same file says it is kept as a record of the 2026-08-29 pass and not an invitation to run another, and line 75 is the launch that pass actually used - repointing it would contradict the reading this plan freezes.

`traktor_nml/README.md`'s own high-water mark reads DL-128, so this plan mints DL-129 through DL-147. Acceptance is a served-page gate run driving `/`, `/reconnect` and `/reconstruct`, judged on what the live page reports, recorded in a new dated record. `docs/2026-08-28-w002-browser-record.md` and `docs/2026-08-29-w004-focus-ring-record.md` are records of runs already taken and keep every byte.

The milestone boundary follows a guard rather than the file types: `tests/test_gui_theme.py:333` requires every `.wizard-*` class the stylesheet defines to reach `app.py`, so `theme.py` lands with the header builder that consumes it, while `navigation.py` - framework-free and waiting on no consumer - keeps a milestone of its own (DL-147).
